title: Module 4 Knowledge Check
description: Eight questions on objectives and aligned assessment. Unlimited attempts; best score counts.

questions.text: Which objective contains all three of Mager's components?
options: Given an e-learning module, participants will identify all WCAG violations from a list of eight common types
The instructor will present the four WCAG principles
questions.feedback: Condition (given a module), performance (identify violations), criterion (all, from a list of eight).

questions.text: Which verbs describe observable performance? Select all that apply.
questions.feedback: Classify, demonstrate, and diagnose are observable. Understand, appreciate, and be familiar with describe internal states.

questions.text: A task analysis shows the job requires applying a procedure. The designer writes objectives at the 'create' level of Bloom's taxonomy to make the course more rigorous. This is:
options: Good practice; higher is always better
Misalignment; the objective level should match the task analysis
Acceptable if the assessment is multiple choice
questions.feedback: The taxonomy is a vocabulary for matching, not a ladder to climb. Objectives derive from the task analysis.

questions.text: In the Dick and Carey model, assessment instruments are developed after the instructional strategy is chosen.
questions.feedback: Assessments come right after objectives and before strategies, to guarantee alignment.

questions.text: An objective asks learners to decide whether a mismatch alert requires stopping. Which assessment is aligned?
options: List the three types of alerts
Given six new scenarios with alerts, decide in each whether to stop, with a rationale
Describe the alert workflow in your own words
questions.feedback: A decision objective needs an assessment that presents decisions, with new scenarios rather than the ones used in instruction.

options: Learners are ranked against each other
Each learner is measured against the standard stated in the objective
Scores are curved to a normal distribution
The instructor sets the passing score after seeing results
questions.feedback: The criterion in the objective is the standard. If many learners fail, examine the instruction.

questions.text: Where should the distractors for a multiple-choice item ideally come from?
options: Common errors identified in the task analysis
questions.feedback: Distractors built from real errors are diagnostic. A distractor nobody chooses is wasted.

questions.text: Which scoring guide describes each criterion at each level of performance?
questions.feedback: Analytic rubrics are the most reliable and give the most useful feedback.
